newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says tunnel to stay open.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says tunnel to stay open.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Saturday that Israel would never close a tunnel beside a Moslem holy site in Jerusalem which triggered Palestinian protests threatening Middle East peace.
"The tunnel has been around for 2,000 years. It will stay open. It will always be open," he said in a speech to 6,000 visiting Christian supporters of Israel.
"Israel doesn't make unilateral concessions any more. It actually demands a quid pro quo," he said.
"It does not speak well of the international community that it accepts this violence...as a legitimate aim...We go towards the path of peace in peace," Netanyahu told the crowd.

Palestinian police kept a lid on protests in most of the West Bank and Gaza on Saturday while U.S. and U.N. officials tried to fix a PLO-Israeli summit to stop the violence which in the past four days has claimed nearly 70 lives.
Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak said earlier: "For the moment there are no specific plans for a meeting."
